hero.source: USS Missouri (BB-63) flyover, Tokyo Bay, 2 September 1945 (80-G-421130)
hero.description: Surrender of Japan, 2 September 1945: U.S. Navy carrier planes fly in formation over the U.S. and British fleets in Tokyo Bay during surrender ceremonies. The battleship USS Missouri (BB-63), where the ceremonies took place, is at left. The light cruiser USS Detroit (CL-8) is in the right distance. Aircraft include Grumman TBM Avenger, Grumman F6F Hellcat, Curtiss SB2C Helldiver and Vought F4U Corsair types.

gallery.title: File:Tanaka Shizuichi.jpg
gallery.artist: Unknown author
gallery.credit: The Philippines Expeditionary Force Information Department Editors (1943-June)       The Philippines Expeditionary Force, Japan:  The Philippines Expeditionary Force Information Department Retrieved on 24 February 2009.
gallery.description: The person in the picture is Shizuichi Tanaka, a famous commander of Imperial Japanese Army in days of World War II. The source book, The Philippines Expeditionary Force, names him "Army Commander Tanaka" without further details. According to the  Japanese Wikipedia article on "Japanese Army uniform", he is wearing a Showa 5 type or M90 uniform with the epaulette of lieutenant-general. Therefore, this picture should be considered to be taken between July 1938 to September 1943.

Potsdamer (Berliner) Konferenz der führenden Staatsmänner der drei alliierten Mächte der UdSSR, Grossbritannien und der USA vom 17. Juli bis 2. August 1945 in Schloß Cecilienhof und Babelsberg. Ihr Ergebnis ist das Potsdamer Abkommen, das die völkerrechtlichen Grundfragen für den Aufbau eines friedlichen, demokratischen deutschen Staates und die Politik der Siegermächte gegenüber Deutschland festlegt.

gallery.title: File:B29 leaflet.jpg
gallery.artist: Mark Pellegrini
gallery.credit: Own work
gallery.description: A leaflet dropped from a B-29 on Japan after the bombing of Hiroshima. Translation: Notice to the Japanese People! Evacuate the city immediately. What this leaflet contains is extremely important, so please read carefully. The Japanese people are facing an extremely important autumn. Your military leaders were presented with thirteen articles for surrender by our three-country alliance to put an end to this unprofitable war. This proposal was ignored by your army leaders. Because of this the Soviet Republic intervened. In addition, the United States has developed an atom bomb, which had not been done by any nation before. It has been determined to employ this frightening bomb. One atom bomb has the destructive power of 2000 B-29s. This frightening fact should be understood by you by observing what kind of situation was caused when only one was dropped on Hiroshima.

gallery.filename: Surrender of Japanese Forces in the Philippines 1945.jpg
gallery.title: File:Surrender of Japanese Forces in the Philippines 1945.jpg
gallery.artist: Jossi at English Wikipedia
gallery.credit: Transferred from en.wikipedia to Commons.
gallery.source: Surrender of Japanese Forces in the Philippines 1945
gallery.description:
Photo #: NH 97276
Surrender of Japanese Forces in the Philippines, 1945
Surrender ceremonies at Baguio, Luzon, on 3 September 1945.
The Japanese commander, General Tomoyuki Yamashita, is seated in the middle on the near side of the table. Seated on the opposite side, second from left, is Lieutenant General Jonathan M. Wainwright, U.S. Army. Toward the right end of the table, immediately to the left of Gen. Yamashita's head, is Commodore Norman C. Gillette, USN, Deputy Commander, Philippine Sea Frontier.

U.S. Naval Historical Center Photograph.
